abstract: The Notch signaling pathway is a central regulator of tissue morphogenesis, yet its output is profoundly context-dependent. We previously demonstrated that Notch coordinates with either the proto-oncogene Src (Notch-Src) or the transcription factor Mef2 (Notch-Mef2) to drive hyperplastic growth and cell proliferation in Drosophila wing imaginal discs via synergistic activation of the JNK pathway. Intriguingly, these two distinct genetic interactions manifest completely divergent apoptotic profiles: Notch-Src activation induces widespread, robust apoptosis, whereas Notch-Mef2 synergy yields minimal cell death, allowing unchecked tissue overgrowth. Because subverting the delicate homeostasis between cell proliferation and programmed cell death is a prerequisite for malignant transformation, we sought to determine the molecular mechanisms underlying this survival advantage. Comparative transcriptomic profiling of Notch-Mef2 versus Notch-Src tissues identified the zinc-finger transcription factors disconnected (disco) and disco-related (disco-r) as specific downstream targets of the Notch-Mef2 axis. We demonstrate that disco and disco-r function in a partially redundant manner as novel anti-apoptotic factors. Their specific induction by the Notch-Mef2-JNK cascade effectively shields hyperplastic tissues from JNK-mediated cell death, providing a novel paradigm for how cooperative transcriptional networks dictate oncogenic outcomes.
